messages.author: 2348a886e6993d13
messages.subject: Using Shapefile to crop Images
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to use the shapefile to crop out each image. I have 9 rows and 4 columns, so a total of 36 plots. I would like to have 36 resulting cropped images of each plot for further analysis in Python. I have tried the function previously given:

plot_clip <- function(ortho, shape){ + plot_raster <- list() + for (i in 1:nrow(shape)) { + cat("plot_", i, " ") + p <- shape[i,] + plot_raster[[i]] <- crop(x = ortho, y = extent(p)) + plot_raster[[i]] <- mask(plot_raster[[i]], p) + names(plot_raster)[i] <- shape$plot[i] + } + return(plot_raster) + }

then
> rasterbyplots <- plot_clip(EX1.RemSoil, EX1.Shape)

but I get the following error:
Error in 1:nrow(shape) : argument of length 0

Have I missed a step somewhere?

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Using Shapefile to crop Images
parts:
Hi William,

Maybe you are using the full output from fieldMask(), which is a list. 

This function requires a single raster per time. 

Try to use EX1.RemSoil$mask (binary output) or EX1.RemSoil$newMosaic (RGB output) instead of only EX1.RemSoil.

Let us know if it works ... ok

All the best,
Filipe

messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Re: Using Shapefile to crop Images
parts:
Hi Wade:
I also used this code to split the image into small plots using shapefile. To save the individual rasterbrick as JPEG photo, you may use the following line of code:

 for(i in 1:length(rasterbyplots)){
    writeJPEG(as.array(rasterbyplots[[i]]), target = paste0("./RGB-mosaic/plots-03-17/",i,".jpg",sep=""),quality = 1)
  }

Best Regards
Tej
